title: Ruby string case conversion can overflow a heap buffer
summary: Changing the case of crafted strings in some single-byte encodings can write one byte past the output buffer. Ruby confirms proof-of-concept code execution in some scenarios.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled strings can reach runtime memory corruption and possible code execution. Reaching the affected encoding and case-conversion path is a prerequisite.

exposure: Applications changing case of untrusted strings in affected encodings, including ISO-8859-1 and Windows-1252, are exposed. The vendor does not establish that every Ruby application reaches the flaw.

params.instructions: Check Ruby version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13 or 4.0.10 on the corresponding line and restart dependent processes.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
